claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was compliant because the due-diligence record showed a material unresolved control risk at the time of decision.
specific_concerns: The governing policy says quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The actor packet itself labels support as weak, which is inconsistent with a locked reject decision.
The summary describes an incomplete and inconsistent diligence record, but does not show that the unresolved issues rose to the policy threshold of material risk required for rejection.
The procurement note appears to recommend follow-up before approval if storage controls remained unresolved; that supports delay/escalation more directly than outright rejection.

Because evidence access is actor-summary-only, there is no way to test whether any cited item is being overstated or whether inadmissible private security-review information influenced the conclusion.
unsupported_claims: The claim that the vendor record contained reject-level material unresolved control risk is not established from the summarized evidence alone.
The claim that the cited quality-process and storage-control issues were sufficient to justify rejection, rather than follow-up or escalation, is unsupported on the provided record.
The statement that price and delivery history did not cure the control concerns may be reasonable, but it does not independently support the stronger reject decision.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual contents of BPROC-009-C, BPROC-009-D, and BPROC-009-E showing the precise control gap, inconsistency, and their severity.
Provide any formally logged due-diligence record that classifies the unresolved issue as material or reject-level under procurement policy.
Provide the procurement approval standard or decision rubric that links these specific unresolved controls to mandatory rejection rather than conditional approval, hold, or escalation.
Confirm whether any private security-review results existed and, if so, whether they were formally logged and admissible.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for vendor rejection based on material unresolved risk.
Treat quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies as support for follow-up or escalation unless there is additional admissible evidence showing reject-level materiality.
Do not credit private security-review results unless they were formally logged and admissible.
Downgrade when the actor packet overclaims beyond what the admissible evidence summary establishes.
